text:
maria_dx: Trying to run redwoodctl for local testing on a fresh Windows 11 VM. Followed README, used the MSI (0.13.0). Installer completed but 'redwoodctl local serve' fails with "no profiles found". I thought setup would create a default profile?

simon_installer: The installer shouldn't overwrite existing profiles but it also doesn't auto-create a default one anymore. We used to, but removed it after some config validation nightmares. Did you accept the telemetry prompt during install? It changes the initial config flow a bit.
maria_dx: I clicked through fast, not sure. Where does it store profiles now?

lina_sre: Profiles are in %APPDATA%\Redwood\profiles.json. Also check %PROGRAMDATA%\Redwood for system-level config if installer was run elevated.
maria_dx: profiles.json missing in both places. There is a redwood.yaml in C:\Users\Default which contains a comment about profile migration.

simon_installer: Hmm. On some corp images the installer runs under SYSTEM during imaging and writes default config into Default user but not the new user's AppData. That explains the files in Users\Default. You can run our small helper to copy defaults into your user dir: 

  powershell -Command "Copy-Item -Path 'C:\Users\Default\AppData\Roaming\Redwood\profiles.json' -Destination \"$env:APPDATA\Redwood\profiles.json\" -Force"

maria_dx: I don't have that Default path on my image. It's a minimal Win11 build.

qa-bot: alert: reproduction steps attached — windows-minimal-image + MSI install + redwoodctl local serve -> exit code 1. Ticket #DX-678 opened.

simon_installer: Ok, another angle: the MSI can skip profile migration if %APPDATA% is not writable at install time. It should show a warning but our UI can be ignored. Can you run the installer again as your user (not admin) using msiexec /i redwoodctl-0.13.0.msi? That forces per-user install path and should populate your %APPDATA%.
maria_dx: I re-ran as non-admin. Installer now shows a toast about per-user install. Still no profiles.json, but redwoodctl now prints a helpful hint: "Run 'redwoodctl profile init' to create a profile". Is that new?

simon_installer: Yes, we added profile init to avoid clobbering. The command will open a browser auth flow if you want to link to hosted. For local serve you can also create a local profile: 

  redwoodctl profile init --name dev-local --local

That creates an ephemeral local token and writes a profile. Note: local tokens expire after 24h by default.

maria_dx: I tried that but login kept failing — it opens browser, I sign in, redirect hits 127.0.0.1:34567 and then redwoodctl says "callback not received". I'm on a corp VPN with split tunneling.

lina_sre: Common issue. Our callback server binds to localhost but Windows firewall or an endpoint security agent (e.g., CrowdStrike) can block the listener, causing the redirect to hang. Two workarounds: (1) use device-code flow: "redwoodctl login --device" or (2) temporarily allow inbound on 127.0.0.1:34567 in firewall.
maria_dx: device flow worked, thanks. But then redwoodctl printed a warning: "auth refresh failed: unexpected 401 on token/refresh" and retried twice then gave up. Local serve still failed.

simon_installer: That refresh bug was seen in 0.12.x and should be fixed in 0.13.1 - we backported a more tolerant retry policy. Are you definitely on 0.13.0?
maria_dx: Yes 0.13.0 MSI. I can try the new exe directly. Where's the canary?

doc_maint: We published a hotfix build: https://staging-releases.redwood.ai/canary/redwoodctl-0.13.1-hotfix.exe (internal). It includes: device-code refresh robustness, clearer firewall troubleshooting, and a small UX change to profile init prompts.

maria_dx: Downloaded and ran the hotfix. Device flow login completed and refresh now succeeds. 'redwoodctl local serve' started, but I'm hitting a permissions error when the binary tries to write a local cache under %LOCALAPPDATA%: "access denied". The VM image locks %LOCALAPPDATA% for some apps.

lina_sre: For blocked local caches we added a config flag to set cache dir: 

  redwoodctl config set cache.path "C:\Temp\redwood-cache"

Try that and restart local serve. We'll file an imaging note for the CI team.

maria_dx: That worked. local serve up and responding. Summary of causes: (1) installer behavior differs depending on elevated vs per-user runs, (2) corp security can block callback/listener and AV/firewall can quarantine installer payloads, (3) token refresh retry was flaky in 0.13.0.

simon_installer: Thanks for the thorough walkthrough. Action items: update README to call out per-user vs system install edge cases, add device-code as recommended workaround for corp environments, and patch MSI to detect when APPDATA is not writable and prompt an explicit migration step. I've created tickets: DX-679 (docs), DX-680 (msi detect), DX-681 (imaging guidance).

doc_maint: I'll update the onboarding guide with a short troubleshooting checklist and a snippet for adding firewall exclusions and using device-code.

maria_dx: Great. Leaving notes in the ticket with exact firewall rule steps and the path locks I saw on the VM. Thanks all :pray:
